title: Josephine Berkeley and the cakewalk
summary: Wooding meets the cakewalk dancer Josephine Berkeley, explains what a cakewalk was, and catches her cake at the Greenwaiters' Ball.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: So what happened now, after that. We're, uh, the rent parties.

Well, we were doin' pretty good at the rent parties.
Well, now, I met a little girl, and this little girl was tryin' to be a singer, too. And Maceo had one, too. So, we used to go up to her house. And she was a little older than we were, and we would play and they would sing.
Well, now, we were beginning to learn keys. But not fast, you know what I mean? The way we played, we was playin' F-sharp and C-sharp, and you couldn't put no singers up there, you see. So, we were getting a little better, now, see. So, at the end of the term I met a woman that was, her name was Josephine Berkeley. She was a dancer, a cakewalk dancer. She was a cakewalker. You know about cakewalk dancers. Do you know about it?
Well, I know about it, yes. Tell me.
Well, cakewalking -- a lot of people, you've heard them say, 'that takes the cake.' A lot of black people say that a lot. 'Man that takes the cake.' Well, where it come from,
they had, they'd do this walkin' dance, and the girls prancin', and the fellow struttin' and all like that. The same thing that George Walker used to do in the show.
Well, the winner would get a big cake. And that was the winner. And maybe a few dollars, maybe ten dollars or something on the side, because that was a lot of money in those days.

So, they would, well this little Josephine, this lady, won the cake. She was a little older than I was. She won the cake, and she was just comin' up, just goin' up the steps in this ball, when it was the Greenwaiters' Ball, One of those musical fun halls. (unintelligible) And she almost dropped this cake. And I grabbed it just in time. Well, we formed a friendship there, see. And, later on, I wanted to get into show business and this lady was in show business, see, so we fell in love. As you'd call it, at least, a fascination, see.
